title: I’m quitting Kindle, and Amazon’s new DRM update proves why you should too
summary: I’m finally ready to leave the Kindle world behind.
body: The Kindle Oasis was released in 2019, and it’s been a while since Amazon added a meaningful update to the system. So, when I learned that Amazon was rolling out a new system software update this past week, I was quite excited. That’s until I learned that the update closes a long-standing loophole for library books borrowed via Libby that lets you hold onto a book longer than you’d otherwise be allowed. Additionally, it further tightens DRM to ensure buyers can’t offload books from the Kindle. While the first feature doesn’t affect me much, the latter, as someone who likes preserving digital media, makes the update an instant no-go for me. On paper, these changes protect publishers’ rights and intellectual property. For the end user, though, they are just another reminder that you never truly own your digital library or even the hardware you technically bought.

Locked chats could let you hide saved ChatGPT conversations from your sidebar, history, and search results behind a PIN or fingerprint. Unlike Temporary Chats, locked chats are designed to stick around, giving users a way to save sensitive conversations without leaving them visible in their regular history. Locked chats could also create a privacy boundary for Memory, letting new information from locked conversations personalize other locked chats without spilling into regular conversations. Your ChatGPT history isn’t necessarily a record that you want to parade around. From the simple math problems that don’t require AI, to asking ChatGPT to craft an email calling in sick for a day off, and from more serious conversations about private projects, to chats about finances, there are plenty of conversations you might want to keep out of others’ line of sight. title: Google is giving you more control over what shows up in your feed
summary: Google's done guessing. You finally get to teach it what you like.
body: TL;DR Google is adding new personalization controls across Search, Discover, and Google News, giving you more say over what content appears. Discover will let you specify topics and links you want to see more of, while Google News on Android will let you customize daily audio briefings around your interests. A new Preferred Source button lets you prioritize your favorite publications, helping their coverage appear across Top Stories, AI Overviews, and AI Mode. Google is pretty good at figuring out what you’re interested in, but it doesn’t always get it right. Read one random story about running, for example, and Discover might suddenly decide you’re training for a marathon. Google is now giving you a little more control over those recommendations across Search, Discover, and Google News. That starts with Discover, where you no longer have to wait for Google to figure out what you like. From the Google app , you can tap the three-dot menu and describe the topics or links you want to see more of in your own words. So, if I’m constantly reading kitchen hacks during my commute, I can ask for more. The same goes for anything from Android phones and photography to football or travel.

title: The wide-screen phone trend is expanding beyond foldables

body: TL;DR HUAWEI has launched the Pura X View, a non-foldable glass-slab phone featuring a wide 16:9.5 aspect ratio for its singular 6.39-inch OLED display. This launch aligns with foldable market trends and previous wide-screen HUAWEI releases such as the Pura X and Pura X Max. Once upon a time, Android phones came in all sorts of shapes and sizes. Over the years, we eventually settled on some common ideals for a smartphone, with a tall 19.5:9 or 20:9 display becoming one of those defining features. Foldables gave the market a chance to experiment, but we settled back on tall book-style and flip-style clamshell foldables. In anticipation of Apple’s iPhone Ultra release, Samsung released the wider-screen Galaxy Z Fold 8 , and its reception has prompted more Android brands to jump onto the wide-screen foldable bandwagon . But what if you don’t want a foldable but still want a wide-screen phone? HUAWEI is answering your prayers with the Pura X View, a new wide-screen glass slab smartphone.

title: This app does with Pixel 11 Pro’s HiLight what Google should have done in the first place
summary: HiLight Studio adds custom colors, light animations, and app notifications to your Pixel 11 Pro's underutilized HiLight LED.
body: TL;DR Google heavily restricted the Pixel 11 Pro’s rear HiLight LED array out of the box, limiting it to Gemini and calls from favorite contacts. The open-source HiLight Studio app unlocks the LED’s full potential with custom app notifications, light patterns (comet, pulse, rainbow), Quick Settings toggles, and built-in hardware protection limits. You can set up the app by sideloading its APK and granting core permissions using Shizuku over Wireless debugging. The Pixel 11 Pro series has a new “HiLight” LED system built around the camera’s flash on the back of the device. HiLight can be used as a notification LED to let you know about calls from your favorite contacts, and it also glows when you’re having a Gemini conversation… and that’s about it. HiLight has plenty of potential, but disappointingly, Google hasn’t blessed it with much functionality out of the box. If you want more out of HiLight and are okay with taking matters into your own hands, the open-source HiLight Studio app supercharges Pixel 11 Pro’s HiLight LED so it’s actually useful.

title: We tested the Pixel 11’s Tensor G6 chip, and the results are brutal
summary: The G6 is better, but not in the ways it needs to be.
body: I’ll be frank, my hopes for the Tensor G6 were mixed coming into the launch of the Pixel 11 series . Google has made meaningful upgrades to the CPU and TPU for traditional app and AI workloads, respectively, while switching to what should be a more efficient modem. But pairing the Pixel 11 Pro with just 12GB of RAM , down from 16GB last year, undermines its high-end AI credentials. Meanwhile, Google has dropped a CPU core from its configuration, reducing the benefits of its more modern architecture. While we can’t blame Google for the current state of the global RAM supply chain, its decision to switch to yet another mid-range graphics chip is harder to defend. Still, now that we have the phone in hand (and managed to get around Google blocking benchmarks via the Play Store), we’ve been able to run our usual suite of benchmarks to get a feel for where the Pixel 11 series falls in the performance pecking order.

title: Android 17’s new distraction-killer is a Pixel 11 exclusive, Google confirms

body: TL;DR Pause Point, Android 17’s new Digital Wellbeing feature to curb time on distracting apps, is limited to Pixel 11. A recently updated support page confirms the feature’s limited availability. While Google does not outright deny the possibility of bringing it to older phones, there’s no certainty yet. It’s often one of those “you vs. you” scenarios when you move to open an app, such as TikTok or Instagram, even without intending to. The realization may not always seep in until several minutes after you’ve used the app, and by then you get caught in a vicious loop of self-loathing and the inability to quit at once. It’s safe to presume it’s the same for (almost) all mere mortals, including me, who need external checks to stop us from opening the app in the first place. And Google may have a trick just for that. With Android 17, Google introduced a new Digital Wellbeing feature to prevent “distracting” apps from hogging all your attention. This new feature, called Pause Point , lets you pause for 10 seconds and deliberate whether you really want to open one of the apps you’ve designated as distracting. title: Waymo’s self-driving cars get Gemini integration, so you have someone to talk to
summary: A new "Zen mode" is coming to Waymo cars as well.
body: TL;DR Waymo has added Gemini integration to its Ojai self-driving cars. Passengers can ask Gemini for information, suggestions, or to pull over the car. It’s also introducing a new triple-screen UI with features like “Zen Mode.” Self-driving cars can be great, especially for introverts who don’t want to talk to anyone on their taxi ride, and Waymo is one of the major companies offering self-driving cabs in the US. Now, the company is trying to make the passenger experience even better with a useful new feature: Gemini integration. The company has announced that it’s finally bringing Gemini to its cars. Passengers can now use Gemini to control things like the music or cabin temperature. They can also ask Gemini for suggestions about the neighborhood they are driving through or get additional information on a monument or building along their route. Additionally, they can request Gemini to pull the car over. However, Gemini cannot control any aspect of the vehicle’s movement or routing, and does not have access to the real-time driving data.
